item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Figuring out how the Stars work was / is an exercise in oblique thinking, since the basis of that entire chunk of the mythos is:

"Hey there's this scip called Star Signals. The Hateful Star is a star that sends out signals. CONNECTION?"

Sauelsuesor got pulled in because, y'know, another talking star, and three is enough for a pattern.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Really cool. I've never given any thought to where Sauelsuesor came from or what she might be.

item.content:encoded: In a small way, yes. I find the Fifthists to be damnably hard to write on the best of days, so it will be a minor role overlapping with the rest of the content, which will be (finally) the inhabitants of this curious little world we call ours. Time for bigfeet!

item.content:encoded: The mythos I'm not skilled enough to elaborate on that I'm building in my head contradicts this one a lot, but that doesn't mean I don't like this a lot. Upvoted with no qualms.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
More mythos stuff. One more to go after this and the basics should be all set down.

This tale was something of a pain to write - all the original drafts were much more in-depth with the Stars and the Fifth Church (not to mention Churches one through four), but they were clunky and awkward and I hated writing them. There might be a little more (Explaining the Main Sequence and the Annie Jump Canon) in the next tale.

Anghammarad is a buried giant, though a far cry from ophite's vision. That I take the blame for.

e: also the hammer of DOOM is a reference to Walt Simonson's Thor run. Best onomatopoeia.
